simple.meaning: שֵׁמַע (shêmaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “something heard , i.e. a sound , rumor , announcement ; abstractly, audience.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 18 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 29:13. Its contexts include family, family line, death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֵׁמַע (H8088).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שֵׁמַע (shêmaʻ) / H8088 is traced through Genesis 29:13, Exodus 23:1, Numbers 14:15, Deuteronomy 2:25 as a generated source-based concept entry.

“You shall not spread a false report. Don’t join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
Now if you killed this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of you will speak, saying,
Today I will begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples who are under the whole sky, who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you.”
When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning Yahweh’s name, she came to test him with hard questions.

When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to test Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great caravan, including camels that bore spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. When she had come to Solomon, she talked with him about all that was in her heart.

Pharaoh’s army had come out of Egypt; and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard news of them, they broke up from Jerusalem.
The king of Babylon has heard the news of them,

There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you; for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?
Yahweh, I have heard of your fame.

definitions.short: something heard , i.e. a sound , rumor , announcement ; abstractly, audience
definitions.usage: bruit, fame, hear(-ing), loud, report, speech, tidings.
definitions.full: H8088. shema I. [ שֶׁ֫מַע noun [masculine] sound ; — שָׁ֑מַע בְּצִלְצְלֵי הַלְלוּהוּ Psa 150:5 (|| תְּרוּעָה ). שֵׁ֫מַע noun [masculine] hearing, report (on from compare Lag BN 143 ); — ׳שׁ absolute Isa 23:5 ; construct 23:5 +; suffix שִׁמְעִי 66:19 etc.; — report , usually with Genitive object: accusative with שְׁמַע Gen 29:13 (J) the tidings about Jacob , Isa 23:5 +? Num 14:15 (JE), Deut 2:25 ; 1Kin 10:1 = 2Chr 9:1 ; Nahum 3:19 ; Hab 3:2 ; Jer 37:5 ; 50:43 ; Isa 66:9 ; with ל Genitive 23:5 ; לַעֲדָתָם Hosea 7:12 usually according to the report (heard by) their congregation (!), but inexplicable and probably corrupt, We Now; Marti (compare Oettli) עַלרָֿעָתָם ( כְּשֵׁמַע as gloss) according to their wickedness ; שׁ ׳נָשָׂא שָׁוְא Exod 23:1 (E) take up (utter) a false report ; ׳לְשׁ אֹוָן Psa 18:45 i.e. as soon as heard of, = mere report Job 42:5 (opposed to personal knowledge), compare שִׁמְעָהּ 28:22 .
